question: In a standard Intensive Care Unit (ICU), what is the usual nurse-to-patient ratio?

options.A: One nurse to four or five patients
options.B: One nurse to one or two patients

explanation: Critically ill patients need close, constant monitoring, which requires a very low nurse-to-patient ratio to keep them safe. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why do nurses in the ICU need to make quick clinical decisions?

options.A: Hospital administrators demand strict paperwork compliance
options.B: Patients can experience sudden and dangerous changes in their health
options.C: Specialized equipment requires constant software updates
options.D: Family members frequently question medical treatments

explanation: Critical care patients are highly unstable, meaning small physical changes can quickly turn into life-threatening emergencies. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h1)

question: In the primary ABCDE assessment framework, what does the letter 'B' stand for?
explanation: The ABCDE framework stands for Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, and Exposure. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h2)

question: If a patient's blood pressure slowly drops over a few hours while their heart rate goes up, what might this mean?

options.A: The patient is getting worse or going into shock
options.D: Normal physiological response to deep sleep

explanation: A faster heart rate is often the body's way of trying to keep blood pressure up when it starts to fall. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the main reason for putting an arterial line in an ICU patient?

options.B: Rapid administration of large volume fluids

explanation: Arterial lines let nurses track blood pressure beat-by-beat and make it easy to draw blood samples for gas analysis. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h3)

question: When are vasopressor medications usually given to a critically ill patient?

options.A: To lower pressure inside the head after a brain injury
options.B: When IV fluids alone fail to bring up blood pressure
options.C: To reverse the effects of anesthesia
options.D: As a routine step before major surgery

explanation: Vasopressors narrow blood vessels to raise blood pressure when fluids are not enough to keep the patient stable. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which nursing action helps prevent pneumonia in patients on a breathing machine?

options.B: Keeping the breathing tube cuff deflated
options.D: Elevating the head of the bed

explanation: Keeping the bed raised between 30 and 45 degrees stops mouth and throat secretions from slipping down into the lungs. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h4)

question: What do arterial blood gas (ABG) tests mainly check in patients on ventilators?

options.C: Pressure inside the brain and blood flow

explanation: ABG results give exact measurements of pH, oxygen, and carbon dioxide to help nurses adjust the ventilator settings. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h4)

question: What three types of responses are measured using the Glasgow Coma Scale?
explanation: The Glasgow Coma Scale checks eye opening, speech, and body movement to measure a patient's level of consciousness. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the main danger of having very high pressure inside the skull (intracranial pressure)?

options.A: Rapid loss of body salts and dehydration
options.B: Decreased production of red blood cells
options.C: Starving brain tissue of oxygen and causing brain shifting
options.D: High blood pressure and swollen limbs

explanation: High pressure inside the skull cuts off blood flow to the brain, starving the tissue of oxygen and risking dangerous brain herniation. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h5)

question: What heart problem is most often linked to low potassium and magnesium levels in the ICU?

options.B: Numbness in the hands and feet

explanation: Potassium and magnesium are needed for the heart's electrical system to work properly, so low levels can trigger dangerous heart rhythms. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why is feeding through the gut (enteral nutrition) usually preferred over IV feeding in critical care?

options.A: It keeps the lining of the intestines healthy and working
options.B: It gets absorbed much faster by the bloodstream
options.C: It requires less monitoring of blood sugar
options.D: It completely removes the risk of infection

explanation: Using the digestive tract keeps the gut lining strong, stops bacteria from leaking out, and supports the immune system better than IV nutrition. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the purpose of using a tool like the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS)?

options.A: To figure out the correct breathing machine settings
options.B: To measure the patient's daily fluid intake and output
options.C: To guide how much sedative or pain medication to give
options.D: To calculate the risk of pressure sores

explanation: The RASS gives nurses a standard way to check how awake or restless a patient is, helping to avoid giving too much or too little medication. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is a major downside of keeping a patient on a ventilator deeply sedated?

options.A: It makes the patient stay on the breathing machine longer
options.B: It immediately gets rid of all risk of confusion
options.C: It stops them from getting used to the drugs
options.D: It always causes permanent memory loss

explanation: Too much sedation delays the process of taking the patient off the ventilator, causes muscle weakness, and keeps them dependent on the machine longer. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which nursing action helps prevent catheter-related urinary tract infections in the ICU?

options.A: Flushing the urinary catheter with antiseptic twice a day
options.B: Giving routine antibiotics to everyone with a catheter
options.C: Changing the urine bag every twelve hours
options.D: Taking out the urinary catheter as soon as it is no longer needed

explanation: Keeping a catheter in for a shorter time is the single best way to prevent urinary tract infections. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h8)

question: Why are immobile ICU patients at high risk for blood clots in their veins?

options.A: The liver stops making clotting factors
options.B: Blood naturally becomes thinner during severe illness
options.C: Arterial pressure places too much demand on deep veins
options.D: Blood pools in the legs because muscles are not contracting

explanation: Without movement, the calf muscles cannot squeeze blood back up to the heart, causing blood to pool and form clots. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h8)

question: What is the main role of the ICU nurse when ethical questions arise about life support?

options.A: Speaking up for what the patient wants and their rights
options.B: Directing the legal team during hospital hearings
options.C: Making the final decision to stop medical treatment
options.D: Persuading family members to agree to aggressive treatment

explanation: Nurses act as patient advocates, making sure that the patient's personal wishes and advance directives guide their care. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h9)

question: What is the most important focus when providing end-of-life care in the ICU?

options.A: Making sure the patient is comfortable and free of pain
options.B: Continuing all lab tests until the moment of death
options.C: Giving lots of fluids to keep blood pressure up
options.D: Limiting family visits to keep the room quiet

explanation: At the end of life, the focus shifts away from trying to cure the disease and centers entirely on comfort, dignity, and managing symptoms. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h9)
